Great questions — answers below. Camila and Marissa are on copy to help with scheduling and technical details.

1) Air-gapped bootstrap credentialing: We support two bootstrap models:
   - Airgap silent bootstrap: you provide a signed offline bundle (no outbound traffic required). An operator on your side runs the install; Redwood provides signed artifacts and installation docs.
   - Staged bootstrap: if you permit temporary outbound to a Redwood package registry for a limited time window we can do an automated install that reduces manual steps.

2) Control plane locality / self-hosting:
   - Redwood Private default: control plane runs in your VPC (private control plane) with operators in your account; control-plane telemetry and management APIs are strictly over private networking.
   - Self-hosted control plane: available as an on-prem package for customers that require complete separation (air-gapped option). This is the model we surface for regulated customers. Difference vs HyperscaleCloud: hyperscalers often retain a managed control-plane with backchanneling for upgrades/metrics; our self-hosted option provides native upgrade tooling but gives you final approval before any change.

We've attached a short matrix (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx) that calls out these exact differentiators. Short answer: you can avoid any outbound calls during runtime and you can opt for full self-hosted control plane for management.

Next steps from here: Camila will propose times for a 45-minute network deep-dive (we'll include an SE to walk your infra and show the bootstrap flow). After that, if you want we'll provide the offline bundle and a test plan for the two tests (non-airgapped latency test, airgapped bootstrap validation).

Thanks,
Vanessa

Hi Jared — thanks for sharing the schematic. A couple of quick technical notes and proposed test plan below.

Quick network notes (based on the attached schematic):
- For the routed VPC (non-airgapped) latency test we'll need:
  * An inbound route from your test subnet to the Redwood inference private endpoint (we will provide IPs).
  * Minimum MTU 1500, and NAT rules allowing backend egress for preflight (only if you choose staged bootstrap).
- For the air-gapped bootstrap:
  * We will provide an offline bootstrap artifact (signed tarball + checksums + install script). Your operators run it in an isolated subnet.
  * Post-install verification does not require outbound connectivity. We do recommend one-way log export to a secure bucket for your own auditing.

Proposed test plan (we can execute over 2 business days):
Day 1 (non-airgapped):
- Small 2-node config, run 10k tokens at 4 concurrent sessions to validate p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput.
- We capture traces and provide a short report.
Day 2 (airgapped bootstrap):
- Provide offline bundle and installation steps to your infra teammate.
- Validate bootstrap completes, run lightweight inference calls locally to confirm model load and KV cache behavior.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-arch.png (annotated for network engineers).

I'll propose slots: Mon 10/5 10:00-10:45 PT, Tue 10/6 14:00-14:45 PT, Wed 10/7 09:00-09:45 PT. Let me know what works and I'll send calendar invites with the runbook.

Cheers,
